research_notes: Initial review 2026-10-01: official frozen four occupation periods retained; primary biography, primary indexed university citation, historical first speech, research biography, newspaper and independent union chronology checked. No roster refresh.

Part-time union work during study is explicit. No transition date to full-time union work and no private-firm full-time evidence found. Do not assume legal qualification, courtroom appearances or professional title establishes continuous full-time employment.

Legal employment must be split between private practice and union employment. Duncan and Hannon dates are year precision, not exactly three years. Without full-time status and precise boundaries/leave, no private full-time range or point estimate is justified. Union and ministerial work excluded under codebook, not recoded as ordinary private/public service.

Open avenues attempted: exact-name employer searches; FWC/AustLII case searches; personal speeches; university citation; research biographies and historical reporting. Broad case searches returned irrelevant namesakes and no dated employment contract. The first speech thanks several unions but does not establish all as employers. Secondary claims of separate CFMEU advisory work in 1995–1996 remain an unresolved lead; avoid duplicate spell until reconciled with Yeadon office.

Source gaps: original Adelaide PDF redirects to staff services, so only indexed content used; personal about-penny URL inaccessible but home biography retrieved; APH direct profile restricted; candidate ABC Q&A URL inaccessible. These are source-level gaps, not run termination.

Follow-up: firm personnel/partnership history and hours, exact 1996/1999 boundaries and leave, union predecessor and 1990–1994 status transition, 1994–1995 gap/possible second union advisory job, 2002 union cessation, earlier paid work and student governance remuneration. Last follow-up 2026-10-01; next Tony Zappia.
